resources.notes: 91 distinct queries, all HTTP 200 (one transient curl exit with HTTP 000 on 'aprinocarsen' was retried and returned 200/total=0). Zenodo has NO deposit pairing oligonucleotide exposure with a platelet endpoint: every platelet/thrombocytopenia x oligonucleotide/antisense/phosphorothioate/siRNA/GPVI/PF4/P-selectin/PAC-1/megakaryocyte cross-query returned total=0 or 1 irrelevant hit. Searches for the named priority compounds oblimersen, G3139, Genasense, drisapersen, GSK2402968, PRO051, aprinocarsen, ISIS 3521, LY900003, ISIS 5132, alicaforsen, ISIS 2302, donidalorsen, TQJ230, viltolarsen, casimersen returned ZERO records of any kind. 'cASO7'/'cASO9'/'cASO11' = 0, so the control-ASO sequences from doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051 Table S2 are not mirrored on Zenodo. All priority NCT numbers returned 0 except NCT01703988 and NCT02052791, which both hit the one nusinersen record. IMPORTANT DEDUP FINDING: Zenodo carries harvested metadata+file MIRRORS of Dryad deposits under the Dryad DOI (record 3901697 = doi:10.5061/dryad.g003051; record 4966673 = doi:10.5061/dryad.n37q406; record 5519880 = doi:10.5061/dryad.1jwstqjs8). These are the SAME deposits as the Dryad rows below, not independent evidence, and must be counted once. The mirrors are operationally valuable because Dryad's own file download is blocked (see Dryad row) while the Zenodo mirror serves the identical PDFs openly. Two Zenodo-native records are AI/aggregator-generated and are NOT primary evidence per rule 5: 10.5281/zenodo.21521124 ('PathMap Experiment #000084', an LLM execution trace from 'Artificial General Intelligence LLC' that matched only because its generated text contains the strings 'antisense oligonucleotide' and 'PF4') and 10.5281/zenodo.19223730 (an auto-generated Trip Database answer page on inotersen thrombocytopenia). Both excluded from candidates.

63 queries, all HTTP 200. Dryad's search is AND-combining, so compound queries are informative: 'oligonucleotide platelet' = 0, 'antisense thrombocytopenia' = 0, 'siRNA platelet' = 0, 'phosphorothioate oligonucleotide' = 0, 'drug induced thrombocytopenia' = 0, 'clinical trial platelet count' = 0. Confirmed by component searches: 'platelet' returns 61 datasets and 'oligonucleotide' returns 43, and the two sets are DISJOINT — there is no Dryad deposit in which an oligonucleotide is applied to platelets. Priority-compound searches oblimersen, drisapersen, mipomersen, inotersen, eteplirsen, alicaforsen, pelacarsen, olezarsen, donidalorsen all returned total=0; only golodirsen (1) and nusinersen (2) exist. The three 2026 ASO deposits that do exist (dryad.6wwpzgn8j huntingtin intron-1, dryad.1vhhmgr7k atrophin-1/DRPLA, dryad.3xsj3txw1 SMN/SMA) are mouse and neuronal-cell CNS efficacy studies with no haematology and no platelet assay — not applicable to this endpoint. Dryad's richest HUMAN in vitro platelet deposit, dryad.fn2z34tpz (Zhou 2020 eLife 10.7554/eLife.52938, 2.94 GB of raw single-platelet-aggregate images across agonists), contains no oligonucleotide arm. NOTE a separate FILE-ACCESS barrier recorded in the Dryad file-download row below: search and metadata are fully open, but file retrieval from Dryad itself is blocked.

resources.barrier_detail: Per-file API download: HTTP 401, body exactly {"error":"Unauthorized, must have current bearer token"} (56 bytes, content-type application/json). Dataset-level /download: identical HTTP 401 + same JSON body. Front-end /downloads/file_stream/414458 and /stash/downloads/file_stream/414458: HTTP 403, 118-byte nginx '403 Forbidden' HTML page. The datasets are CC0-1.0 and publicly listed, so this is a technical/authentication block on the download tier of this environment's egress path, not a licence restriction. No account was created and no credentials were supplied (rule 4).
resources.notes: WORKAROUND FOUND AND USED, so no evidence was lost: both wanted files are mirrored on Zenodo under the same Dryad DOI and download openly there (HTTP 200). Zenodo 4966673 serves 'Darras Online Supplementary appendix.pdf' at 217409 bytes with md5 a9b367826390a4cc8b4723a7d01338e9, byte-identical to the md5 Dryad reports for its own copy — verified same file. Zenodo 3901697 serves '4053-101_FrankD_Dryad_Repository101119.pdf' (448506 bytes, md5 fe40c8fb2877536c52dc0cc7ef752b3e); Dryad's current v14 file is named ...061820.pdf (447646 bytes, sha256 67418e4fcc3aa3cd96a789db709e010e5a66ba850ffdeaf7c6b720b53dbb44eb), i.e. the Zenodo mirror is an EARLIER version of the same supplement (Oct 2019 vs Jun 2020 stamp). Content was checked and the difference is immaterial here because neither version contains haematology data at all. The 2.94 GB dryad.fn2z34tpz archive was deliberately not attempted: it is blocked by the same 401 and contains no oligonucleotide arm.

resources.resource: Zenodo — oligonucleotide-safety / toxicology dataset deposits (targeted sub-sweep)
resources.notes: All eight queries HTTP 200, total=0 in every case. There is no oligonucleotide class-safety or oligonucleotide-toxicology dataset deposit on Zenodo, and no deposit answering to the challenge's own name ('OligoTox' = 0 hits). This is a genuine absence confirmed by real queries, not a barrier. Consequence for the challenge: neither repository in this family holds a sequence+chemistry+toxicity matrix of the kind the OligoTox dataset is being built from; that material lives in journal supplements and regulatory filings, not in these generalist repositories.

candidates.authors_year: Frank DE, Schnell FJ, Akana C, El-Husayni SH, Desjardins CA, Morgan J, et al. (deposit 2020; article 2020)
candidates.discovered_via: Dryad API search q=golodirsen and q=exon skipping; independently surfaced as Zenodo mirror record 3901697 via Zenodo API q=golodirsen

candidates.required_file: 4053-101_FrankD_Dryad_Repository061820.pdf (Dryad v14, 447646 bytes) / 4053-101_FrankD_Dryad_Repository101119.pdf (Zenodo mirror, 448506 bytes) — RETRIEVED via Zenodo mirror
candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: PARTIAL / NOT the platelet gap. Honest assessment after reading the retrieved file: this is the only open patient-level deposit for a PMO (the challenge's named neutral-backbone comparator class) in either repository, but it contains NO haematology. Sections are A) PK methodology, B) exon-skipping RT-PCR, C) immunofluorescence, D) e-tables e-1 to e-7, E) e-figures e-1 to e-4. e-1 = patient mutations and mutation-specific PCR primer amplicon sizes; e-2 = golodirsen plasma PK parameters; e-3 = dose proportionality by exposure ratio; e-4 = golodirsen recovered in urine by collection interval; e-5 = urinary kinetic parameters to 24 h; e-6 = western blot imputation; e-7 = differences in duration of golodirsen exposure between treated patients. Grep for platelet|thrombocyt|PLT|haematolog|hematolog|coagulat returned ONE hit, and it is the phrase 'Bio-Rad Laboratories' — a false positive. Grep for adverse|safety|treatment-emergent returned ZERO hits. What it DOES close: human systemic exposure (plasma Cmax/AUC, dose proportionality, urinary recovery) for a neutral-backbone PMO at 4/10/20/30 mg/kg, which is the quantitative exposure anchor needed to put the PMO class on the same exposure axis as the PS compounds when arguing backbone dependence of thrombocytopenia.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: ~12 patients x 4 dose levels of plasma PK parameters (e-2/e-3) plus urine recovery intervals (e-4/e-5); 0 platelet observations.

candidates.full_title: Analysis code and figures for the olezarsen FAERS/EudraVigilance pharmacovigilance study
candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: Olezarsen is a named priority target, and this is the only open olezarsen safety-analytics deposit found. CAVEAT the curation team must weigh: it is post-marketing spontaneous-report disproportionality (ROR, IC025, logistic regression, E-value/QBA) over FAERS + EudraVigilance, so any thrombocytopenia content is a reporting-rate signal, NOT measured platelet counts, and it cannot supply per-subject platelet values. The manuscript is described as 'submitted' to Therapeutic Advances in Drug Safety, so the underlying article is not yet a verifiable peer-reviewed identifier; the deposit itself is citable. Its reusable element is the derived FAERS/EudraVigilance case counts for olezarsen by preferred term, which could corroborate (not quantify) an olezarsen thrombocytopenia signal.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: Aggregate AE case counts / disproportionality statistics per preferred term; 0 per-subject platelet counts; 0 in vitro observations.

notes: RESOURCE FAMILY: repositories (Zenodo + Dryad). Both services were fully reachable for SEARCH and METADATA: 91 Zenodo queries and 63 Dryad queries all returned HTTP 200, with one transient curl-level failure (HTTP 000 on Zenodo q=aprinocarsen) that was retried to a clean HTTP 200/total=0. One real barrier: Dryad's FILE-DOWNLOAD tier is blocked (HTTP 401 'Unauthorized, must have current bearer token' on both /api/v2/files/<id>/download and /api/v2/datasets/<doi>/download; HTTP 403 nginx on /downloads/file_stream/<id>), recorded as a technical_block. That barrier cost nothing, because Zenodo mirrors the two wanted CC0 Dryad files under their Dryad DOIs and served both at HTTP 200. HEADLINE RESULT, stated plainly: NEITHER REPOSITORY CONTAINS ANY DATASET IN WHICH AN OLIGONUCLEOTIDE IS APPLIED TO PLATELETS. In Dryad this is demonstrable rather than merely unobserved: q=platelet returns 61 datasets, q=oligonucleotide returns 43, Dryad's search is AND-combining, and q='oligonucleotide platelet' returns 0 — the two sets are disjoint. In Zenodo every platelet/thrombocytopenia crossed with oligonucleotide/antisense/phosphorothioate/siRNA/GPVI/PF4/P-selectin/PAC-1/megakaryocyte/washed-platelets/PRP returned total=0. So ZERO human in vitro oligonucleotide-platelet candidates exist in this family, which is the single most decision-relevant finding here: the Phase-2-preferred evidence class is absent from both generalist repositories and the curation effort should not be resourced against them. COMPOUND COVERAGE: oblimersen/G3139/Genasense, drisapersen/GSK2402968/PRO051, aprinocarsen/ISIS 3521/LY900003, ISIS 5132, alicaforsen/ISIS 2302, donidalorsen, pelacarsen/TQJ230, viltolarsen and casimersen have NO deposit of any kind in either repository. Only two priority-relevant human deposits exist at all (golodirsen, nusinersen), both CC0, both retrieved — and, after reading them, BOTH CONTAIN NO PLATELET OR HAEMATOLOGY DATA. I verified this rather than inferring it from titles: the golodirsen supplement greps to zero hits for adverse|safety|treatment-emergent and its only platelet-regex hit is the false positive 'Bio-Rad Laboratories'; the nusinersen appendix mentions haematology only in two exclusion-criterion lines. A reader scanning titles would reasonably assume 'Dryad golodirsen patient data' supplies PMO-class platelet counts. It does not. What golodirsen does supply is human plasma/urine PK and dose-proportionality for a neutral-backbone PMO (e-tables e-2 to e-5), useful as the exposure axis for a backbone-dependence argument, not as a platelet endpoint. The nusinersen deposit's residual value is that it adds two NCT-verified trials (NCT01703988 CS2, NCT02052791 CS12, both COMPLETED) outside the challenge's named NURTURE/SHINE/DEVOTE set. DEDUPLICATION, as the family guidance required: Zenodo harvests Dryad deposits and republishes them under the Dryad DOI, so Zenodo record 3901697 = doi:10.5061/dryad.g003051, record 4966673 = doi:10.5061/dryad.n37q406, record 5519880 = doi:10.5061/dryad.1jwstqjs8. These are 3 deposits, not 6, and the candidates list carries each once with the mirror noted. Version caveat: the Zenodo golodirsen mirror is an EARLIER file version (...101119.pdf, 448506 B) than Dryad's current v14 (...061820.pdf, 447646 B); immaterial here since neither holds haematology. EXCLUDED AS NON-PRIMARY under rule 5: 10.5281/zenodo.21521124 (an LLM execution trace deposited by 'Artificial General Intelligence LLC', matching only because its generated prose contains 'antisense oligonucleotide' and 'PF4') and 10.5281/zenodo.19223730 (an auto-generated Trip Database answer on inotersen thrombocytopenia). Neither is evidence despite indexing as a Zenodo 'dataset'/'publication' on an on-target topic. ALSO SEARCHED AND ABSENT: the control ASOs cASO7/cASO9/cASO11 (0 hits on Zenodo, so Table S2 of doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051 is not mirrored here); Sewing 2017 and Slingsby 2022 raw/per-donor data (no author or title deposit in either repository); all priority NCT numbers except the two nusinersen ones; and any oligonucleotide class-safety or toxicology matrix ('OligoTox' itself returns 0). NOT APPLICABLE rather than empty: the three 2026 Dryad ASO deposits (dryad.6wwpzgn8j huntingtin, dryad.1vhhmgr7k atrophin-1/DRPLA, dryad.3xsj3txw1 SMN) are mouse/neuronal CNS-efficacy studies with no haematology arm, and dryad.xpnvx0kk9 is LC-MS/MS primary-structure mapping of an mRNA vaccine, not an ASO and with no platelet readout — relevant to chemical-characterisation METHOD, not to this endpoint. NO account was created, nothing was purchased, no credentials were supplied and no authors were contacted. Two files were written to research_staging; no other file was modified.
